items.body: Review by arymenezes — This extraordinary box set deserves a comprehensive review. Moreover, purchasing an item of this magnitude is a significant financial decision for many people, so a detailed review can help upon the choice of buying it or not.CD1It's the studio version of "Heavy Horses", with several bonus tracks of demos recorded between 1977 and 1978.Track 1 is dynamic, with good flute and guitar work. The rhythm section is a bit random, with some mismatched time signatures. At the very end, the vocal harmonies are fantastic, and everything fits together very well. Track 2 starts dynamically, then turns into a pop-rock tune with slight folk touches. There's even a brief, well-crafted interlude in the middle, with clapping, flute, and percussion. At the very end, it becomes repetitive. Great guitar intro on the 3rd track, followed by a splendid blues-rock combination involving bass and drums. Good development of the main ideas. Up to 2min, it gains good dynamism and great acceleration. The support of the guitar, even when it's more in the background, is always vigorous and essential. At 4 and a half minutes they return to an inventive blues-rock. This time, with a little more presence of the strings. A good ballad on the 4th track is complemented by a smooth focus on vocal rhythms, performed with a fabulous pitch. The flute phrasing that underlines the vocals also sets the tone for the strings. Enchanting. In the middle there is an efficient interlude. The bass and vocals are somewhat disjointed from each other in the next song. The drums do a good job, but they're also a bit lost. There's no captivating or remotely memorable melody. Furthermore, there's a time signature, quite omnipresent in this composition, that is irritating and simplistic. The strings don't save the main phrases of the 6th track, which are extremely pedantic. But at least they prevent this composition from being even worse. There's a beautiful guitar piece on the 7th track, however everything else is almost childish. The vocals are particularly repetitive and limited. The first half of the 8th track is a mediocre ballad, but are slightly compensated by velvety vocals. From the middle onwards it speeds up a bit, taking on a medieval and concomitantly rock-ish flavor. There's nothing particularly noteworthy, but it's listenable. 10th track offers a strong rhythmic approach, featuring a good blend of cymbals, bass, and strings. Ian's vocals flow with clarity and personality, remaining naturally consistent. The next song is an intricate mix of folk ideas?somewhat raw and slightly disjointed. It could have been a great track had they worked on it a bit more. Track 12 is a good ballad, with beautiful vocal and guitar works. It's almost a copy of one of the acoustic tracks from Aqualung. Doesn't end well. Next song has well-crafted harmonies and a striking looping march. However, it has the same problem as the previous demo regarding the ending, which makes it less memorable than many other Jethro tunes. The guitar contributions on the 14th track are worthwhile, though the choices regarding when to include them were poorly executed. There is a fine interplay between acoustic guitar, flute, and percussion throughout much of this piece of music. The 15th track, "Beltane," is fantastic! It features inventive and amazing vocal harmonies. In fact, everything comes together beautifully and is a delight to the ears. There are some inventive drum patterns and incredible flute "attacks". According to the booklet in the box set, this song was recorded in July 1977 and was intended for the (never-released) 'Moths' EP. It was also considered for the B-side of the "Moths" single, but they ultimately opted for the 1971 track "Life Is a Long Song". The booklet testifies that Beltane first appeared on a release in the 1988 box set '20 Years of Jethro Tull'. Piano and vocals open the 16th track. It is a song with a romantic feel (note: unrelated to the Romantic era). Strings and flute add beautiful contours to the other instruments and also shine when taking the lead in the composition. 17th track: the vocals are expressive, and the acoustic guitar is well forged, without becoming excessive. The flute nicely frames the composition here and there. Strings flow with a sense of youthfulness and elegance. The 18th track is neither good nor bad ? ok, but unremarkable.CD 2In short, both this disc and disc 3 capture a concert performed by JT at the Bern Festhalle in Switzerland on May 28, 1978. Five of the twenty-four tracks from the tapes of this show were used for Bursting Out (with the remaining material sourced from other European concerts). However, as Martin notes in the booklet, Bursting required numerous overdubs to become "presentable". Based on my listening to these CDs of the Swiss show, there are far fewer overdubs here. And the performances are MAGNIFICENT! A listener might complain about songs, regarding his/her personal preferences, but I'd bet high that everyone agrees they're playing at the top of their game!The first track is a classical-style introduction ? albeit with sinister, dramatic touches ? that takes on a playful tone towards the end. Track 2 features a master of ceremonies announcing the show. Track 3 rocks! What chemistry between the guitar and flute! The guitar tones are outstanding, and the drumming is precise, combining economy and power with wonderful artistry. The vitality and sensitivity of all the musicians are immediately apparent. Towards the end, the bass wonderfully drives the track. Track 4 features good guitar riffs, but the rest of the instrumentation doesn't really pop up so high-levelled. It ends in a very loose, unstructured way. Track 5 is a spectacular rendition of the classic "Skating Away on the Thin Ice of the New Day". All the instrumental elements from the original studio version are present, and the bass delivers a magnificent performance, adding a firmer layer of groove. Track 6 is a song I love. The guitar is clear and eloquent. Ian's vocals are incredibly powerful, always remaining fresh and at the right pitch. Well, they didn't perform the entire song, but it's ok, 'cause the quality of the entire presentation is highly remarkable. The harmony of the 7th track initially surprised me, especially for a Heavy Horses song. The music grows in density, transitioning to gentler sections, with good time signatures. The timing of the vocals is less impressive this time. Furthermore, in general, it's a song with slower rhythms, but it lacks the elements that captivate in a slow song. They move on to the title track from the 1978 release. Martin Barre delivers great timbres and marks the notes very well. The rest of the band performs their work perfectly, but what really doesn't help is that the composition is limited. They finished the song very well. On the ninth track, they reach way back to 1969 for a standout blues-rock song from their career: "It Was a New Day Yesterday". With Ian's evolution on the flute, Martin's superb improvement since those early days, and the remaining spectacular lineup, what you hear is nothing short of a powerfull performance. The next track is well-known to Jethro fans, as it appears on Bursting Out. It features a blistering flute solo followed by an exquisite rendition of "God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen/Bourr�e". It speaks for itself; if you haven't heard it yet, give it a listen, dear reader. The eleventh track is a heavier, fully instrumental version of "Living in the Past" blended with "A New Day Yesterday." Unforgettable! The twelfth track features a sublime performance. You can tell the band members are a bit tired, yet they still deliver a beautifully polished gem. After all ? at least to my ears ? "Songs from the Wood" boasts the most exceptional and brilliant vocal harmonies in Tull's entire body of work. Anderson's stamina is impressive, demonstrating such vigor on the flute throughout this sequence of songs (which may not reflect the actual setlist order from the concert, but damn it, it's nice to think it does).CD 3JT always took great care of Thick as a Brick's live performances, and the opening of this disc wasn't different. Therefore, you'll hear 13 minutes of pure delight. They start off brilliantly in Hunting Girl. In fact, they manage to reproduce with accuracy and splendid firmness that truly difficult sequence of bass, guitar, flute, alternating, stopping, returning. Wow, holy gods of musicianship, I was already enchanted when I saw them live here on my city. But in this 1978 recording, they were even several steps above. All the layers and even extra nuances were there, and fortunately, they were recorded and rearranged by the brilliants Steven Wilson and Jakko Jakszyk. They gave Too Old to Rock and Roll, the 3rd track, a slightly naive feel, which was positive, as it gained in fluidity. From the halfway point onwards, the music gains speed, making it even more engaging. The following song, Conundrum, is also on Bursting Out. It's an entirely instrumental experience with a dense sonic mass, based on guitar and drums. A power trio proposal. Intense, but it just lacks a bit of identity. The 5th track has an intense and perfect Minstrel in the Gallery vibe. The guitar is penetrating, and the rock chords paints an impressive sonic density on the whole thing. Besides, Jethro knew very well that shows have to give ROCK AND ROLL to the audience. In the 6th track, the sonic mass is impressive, both in the opening, with extra layers in the instrumental, and also with the unstoppable Martin Barre! To me, it sounds like he is being, in the performance of this song, the inspiration for the others, making everyone, including Anderson, surpass themselves. Shortly after the halfway point, the drummer and bassist seem to think "hey, I'm not going to let the guitarist overshadow me!", and the grow on technique and passion. Exuberant!! The seventh track is a delightful march led by a keyboard-guitar combination. Fantastic. It serves as the prelude to the eighth track, "Aqualung," which kicks off in a truly menacing fashion! The timing is astonishingly good?both regarding the "sluggish" feel of many sections and the transitions between different harmonic structures. They even managed to improve upon the song's conclusion (a part of the original studio version I consider "merely good"). Then comes JT's flagship track, "Locomotive Breath," this time leaning even further into blues and, especially, jazz. When Barre enters, his playing is piercing and deeply inspired! The heavier section of the composition feels even heavier this time ? so much so that the flute gets a bit buried within that dense wall of sound. Right at the end, there is a brief improvisation that serves as a lead-in to the next song, the tenth track: initially a pompous march, it quickly shifts into a vibrant, full-on rock vibe rich with particularly intense nuances. Towards the end, it brilliantly morphs back into a reprise of "Aqualung".DVDsDVD 1 contains the studio album's original stereo mix, as well as Steven Wilson's 5.1 surround remix. I could listen to the former but not the later; I then changed the audio settings, and the sound came through. Therefore, be aware of the sound configuration of your DVD player. Accompanying this audio are images from the studio, the sound engineer, parts of the vinyl liner notes, and footage of instruments, tour travel, backstage moments, etc. As for the difference between the original mix and Mr. Wilson's, he did what is expected of a good engineer: he opened up the instrument separation without sounding excessive. But he didn't do "only" that. On the song "Lullaby", for instance, he turned the bass down slightly and balanced it better with the other instruments so it wouldn't stand out too much?which is what happens in the 1978 version. And on "Journeyman", I noticed right away that the bass is more prominent and has a slightly more metallic tone in this mix. This DVD includes extras, such as a superbly recorded version of the track "Rover" without the string section. There is also another version of "Living in These Hard Times" and the spectacular song "Beltane," which does not appear on the original release of any studio album until 1978.The video content on DVD 2 begins with photos of the 1978 tour. There are duplicated fotos ? some repeated more than once.The video and audio quality of the promotional clips for "Heavy Horses" and "Moths" are exceptional. It is always satisfying to see Ian's wild, boyish face and his almost flamboyant mannerisms. In "Heavy Horses", the whole band appears playing, whereas "Moths" features only the group's leader. The string arrangements on both songs are excellent, although the song about horses feels a bit repetitive to me and could have been shortened. Another bonus video is the promotional (brief, of course) clip for the double album Bursting Out, as well as the short promo video that features both the advertisement for Bursting Out and the announcement of the Madison Square Garden concert.BOOKLETIt contains informationS about the tracks on CD1, original studio credits, dedications, and technical recording details. It also has acknowledgments for the box set edition, as well as additional information regarding the artwork, recording, and production.Drawing on accounts from Ian, Martin, and Dee Palmer (formerly David; the new name was adopted following a gender transition), it also discusses the studio built under Ian's direction ? Maison Rouge ? which, according to its creator, remained in operation for only a few years after the Heavy Horses sessions. The booklet features commentaries ? particularly from these three (former) members ? on the somber atmosphere surrounding the band (and, by extension, the album itself) at the time. Each one of them offers their own theories on the matter, with Dee Palmer's analysis being particularly interesting, including comparisons to the creative and recording processes of other releases. There is also a section dedicated to the numerous demos recorded between 1977 and 1978 (some of which appear as bonus tracks on CD1) and the reasons why they were not ultimately used. So far, I have read 17 of the booklet's 93 pages in full.However, I have leafed through the rest of the content and can say there is a wealth of fascinating information?such as Darryl Way's accounts of his collaborations with JT, details on the UK tour, Ian's recollections regarding each track on Heavy Horses, and a chronology of the era. Last but not least, the song lyrics.About the rating of the box. I don't enjoy Heavy Horses, and that's why I sadly won't give it a 5 stars. My choice is for a 4.8.

items.body: The Danse Society’s reunion album “Change of Skin” turns 15 this year. The English gothic rock band released the record on 18 July 2011 through their own Society Records, its first studio album in 25 years and the first to feature a new lead vocalist, Maethelyiah, in place of founding singer Steve Rawlings. The reunion began with a Facebook campaign, The Danse Society Reformation Plot, launched at the end of 2009. Guitarist Paul Nash, drummer Paul Gilmartin and keyboardist David Whitaker agreed to reform the band, and Rawlings initially joined them, recording instrumental sessions with the group over the following months. In October 2010 Rawlings met the band in the UK and recorded vocals for one track, “Towers”, before contact with him broke down. In January 2011, Maethelyiah, previously of the band Blooding Mask, joined The Danse Society and recorded vocals for all 13 tracks that became “Change of Skin”. “Change of Skin” was issued on CD in a Digipak with printed lyrics and artwork for each song. The tracklist runs “Revelation”, “Change of Skin”, “God Cry”, “Black Dream”, “Slowfire”, “Fornification”, “Let Me Sleep”, “Resurrection”, “Embrace of the Ice Swan”, “Vatican”, “Homelands”, “Sinking” and “End of Days”. The album was written and produced by the band, with Gilmartin on drums and percussion, Nash on guitar and bass, Whitaker on keyboards and Maethelyiah on vocals. The band released “God Cry” as the album’s first single in November 2011, followed in April 2012 by “Vatican”, backed with a reworked version of their 1982 song “Seduction”. The Danse Society played their first live show in 25 years at Germany’s Wave-Gotik-Treffen festival in May 2012, followed by a run of festival dates. About The Danse Society The Danse Society formed in Barnsley, England, in 1980, initially performing as Y? and then Danse Crazy before settling on their permanent name. The original lineup paired singer Steve Rawlings with guitarist Paul Nash, keyboardist Lyndon Scarfe, bassist Tim Wright and drummer Paul Gilmartin. The band pressed its first single, “Clock”, on its own newly formed label, Society, in 1980, reaching number 11 on the UK Indie Chart. Their debut album, “Seduction”, followed in 1982 and reached number 3 on the UK Indie Chart. Scarfe left after that album and was replaced by David Whitaker, formerly of Music for Pleasure. The band’s second album, “Heaven Is Waiting”, came out in December 1983 on Arista Records and reached number 39 on the UK Albums Chart; it included a cover of The Rolling Stones’ “2000 Light Years from Home”. In 1985, at their label’s request, the band recorded the single “Say It Again” with producers Stock, Aitken and Waterman. The Danse Society released its third album, “Looking Through”, in 1986 under the name The Danse Society International. Afterward, every member except Rawlings left to form Johnny in the Clouds. Rawlings continued using the Society name, releasing the single “Saturn Girl” in 1987 before moving on to the project Meridian Dream. The band reformed at the end of 2009 through the Facebook campaign The Danse Society Reformation Plot, reuniting Nash, Gilmartin and Whitaker. Rawlings took part in early sessions and one demo vocal before departing the project; Maethelyiah, formerly of Blooding Mask, took over vocal duties and completed the reunion album “Change of Skin”, released on 18 July 2011 as the band’s fourth studio album. The band followed it with singles “God Cry” (2011) and “Vatican” (2012) and returned to the stage in May 2012 at Germany’s Wave-Gotik-Treffen festival. The Danse Society went on to release “Scarey Tales” (2013), “VI” (2015), the EP “The FUTUR1ST” (2018), “Sailing Mirrors” (2020) and “The Loop” (2024), with the lineup changing several times along the way. Founding drummer Paul Gilmartin, who played on “Seduction” and “Heaven Is Waiting” and remained with the reformed band until 2014, died on 6 August 2024. Fifteen years after its release, “Change of Skin” remains the record that reintroduced The Danse Society and set the band’s post-reunion course. Change of Skin by The Danse Society

items.body: Brooklyn-founded, Los Angeles-based synth act Black Marble has released the single “Anything”, with a video directed by Scott Kiernan. The track is the latest preview of the album “Life in Small Spaces,” due August 21, 2026 on Sacred Bones Records. Black Marble is the solo project of Chris Stewart. “Anything” is built on dry drums, chiming guitar and keyboards, a leaner arrangement than earlier Black Marble releases. Stewart describes the track’s theme in terms of modern relationships and constant options: “Anything is basically a bedroom pop version of Satisfaction but it trades the carnal undertones for more of a domestic pastiche,” says Stewart. “…the center of the struggle is less about finding temporary satisfaction, but that today’s glut of options and opportunities gives every relationship an expiration date, every encounter an easy off ramp and every minor annoyance a reason to move on. The sentiment is the same from those old days, lack of fulfillment, but it’s due to modern circumstances. It feels like we have every option at our fingertips but we’re somehow losing the ability to connect.” Kiernan’s video was shot at Various/Artists in New York City and shows Stewart at the center of a fast-moving accumulation of images. Anything by Black Marble Black Marble ‘Life in Small Spaces’ tour dates Black Marble tours North America from August 22 through September 19, 2026 in support of “Life in Small Spaces”: Saturday, August 22 – Santa Ana, CA – Constellation Room at the Observatory Sunday, August 23 – Los Angeles, CA – 1720 Tuesday, August 25 – San Francisco, CA – Rickshaw Stop Wednesday, August 26 – Sacramento, CA – Harlow’s Friday, August 28 – Seattle, WA – The Crocodile Saturday, August 29 – Portland, OR – Wonder Ballroom Sunday, August 30 – Boise, ID – Shrine Social Club Monday, August 31 – Salt Lake City, UT – Urban Lounge Tuesday, September 1 – Denver, CO – The Federal Theatre Thursday, September 3 – Omaha, NE – Slowdown Friday, September 4 – Minneapolis, MN – Fine Line Saturday, September 5 – Chicago, IL – Thalia Hall Sunday, September 6 – Detroit, MI – El Club Monday, September 7 – Toronto, ON – Lee’s Palace Tuesday, September 8 – Montreal, QC – La Sala Rosa Thursday, September 10 – New York City, NY – Webster Hall Friday, September 11 – Philadelphia, PA – Union Transfer Saturday, September 12 – Baltimore, MD – Ottobar Monday, September 14 – Raleigh, NC – Kings Tuesday, September 15 – Atlanta, GA – The Earl Thursday, September 17 – Houston, TX – White Oak Music Hall Upstairs Friday, September 18 – Dallas, TX – Club Dada Saturday, September 19 – Austin, TX – 29th Street Ballroom Pre-orders for “Life in Small Spaces” are available through Sacred Bones Records. About Black Marble Chris Stewart founded Black Marble in Brooklyn in 2011, initially alongside Ty Kube of Team Robespierre. The project’s debut full-length, “A Different Arrangement,” arrived October 9, 2012, on Hardly Art, the Sub Pop imprint that signed Stewart after he had posted a single song online. “It’s Immaterial,” Black Marble’s second album, followed in October 2016 on Ghostly International and marked Kube’s departure from the project. Stewart signed to Sacred Bones Records and relocated from Brooklyn to Los Angeles around the release of Black Marble’s third album, “Bigger Than Life,” on October 25, 2019. “I Must Be Living Twice,” a covers EP featuring reworked songs originally by Wire, Robert Palmer and Grouper, followed in August 2020. Black Marble’s fourth full-length, “Fast Idol,” arrived October 22, 2021, also on Sacred Bones. “Anything,” released July 17, 2026, previews Black Marble’s fifth album for Sacred Bones, “Life in Small Spaces,” due August 21, 2026. Stewart supports the release with a North American tour running from late August through September 2026.

items.body: Detroit industrial-punk duo Credit Card has released its debut single, “Harsh Times”, the first track from the upcoming collection “Devil’s Night / Dead Internet.” The single arrived July 15, 2026, self-released through Bandcamp. The project consists of Shaun Hunter, who handles vocals, synth and noise, and Max Dameron, who works programming, synth and guitar. “Harsh Times” is built around a hard-driving beat and processed, distorted electronics under Hunter’s vocals. The band is readying “Devil’s Night / Dead Internet” as a debut “mixtape,” set for release in Summer 2026. Harsh Times by Credit Card “Harsh Times” is available to stream and order on Bandcamp. About Credit Card The Detroit project was formed by Shaun Hunter and Max Dameron. Hunter handles vocals, synth and noise; Dameron works programming, synth and guitar. “Harsh Times,” released July 15, 2026, is the pair’s first released single and the opening track from their upcoming debut collection, “Devil’s Night / Dead Internet,” due in Summer 2026. No further formats or dates for the release have been confirmed.

items.body: Los Angeles post-punk band Cure For Youth has announced its debut album, “Synthetic World”, led by the single “New Rose Bloom” and an accompanying video released July 18, 2026. A release date for the album has not been announced. Cure For Youth is a Los Angeles quartet: Scott Savarie plays bass and sings, Nicolas Sturz plays drums, Connor McKenna plays guitar and Catarina Teles plays synthesizer. “Synthetic World” runs twelve songs across thirty-five minutes. Alex Jacobelli recorded and mixed the album at Sunsick Studios; Andrew Oswald handled mastering. A full tracklist has not been published. ‘New Rose Bloom’ video and lyrics The video for “New Rose Bloom” moves through Los Angeles in short, uneven cuts: sidewalks, storefronts, passing cars, domestic footage and protest scenes appear without a fixed hierarchy between them. The lyrics describe a narrator caught in a repeating cycle of survival, disappointment, aging and loss, with brief moments of renewal that lead back to the same pattern. New Rose Bloom by Cure For Youth “New Rose Bloom” and “Synthetic World” are available to stream and order on Bandcamp. About Cure For Youth Cure For Youth is a post-punk quartet from Los Angeles built around Scott Savarie on bass and vocals, Nicolas Sturz on drums, Connor McKenna on guitar and Catarina Teles on synthesizer. The band released the two-track EP “Life Without Loss,” featuring the title track and “Silence,” on June 20, 2024, through Bandcamp. “New Rose Bloom,” released July 18, 2026, is the first single from the band’s debut full-length, “Synthetic World.” The album was recorded and mixed by Alex Jacobelli at Sunsick Studios and mastered by Andrew Oswald, and is set to run twelve songs over thirty-five minutes. A release date has not yet been confirmed. The single and its video mark the next step in Cure For Youth’s catalogue since the 2024 EP.

items.body: Liverpool post-punk band Echo & The Bunnymen have announced “Apples for Isaac”, their thirteenth studio album and first collection of newly written songs since 2014’s “Meteorites.” The album arrives September 18, 2026, on BMG. Its first single, “Brussels Is Haunted,” is out now. Ian McCulloch and Will Sergeant, the band’s founding vocalist and guitarist, lead the current lineup. “Brussels Is Haunted” received its first radio play on BBC Radio 6 Music from Chris Hawkins before its streaming release. Drums on the track, and on ten of the album’s eleven songs, were played by Clem Burke of Blondie, recorded before his death in April 2025. Echo & The Bunnymen dedicated the album to Burke, calling him “integral to the making of the album” and closing with the message “Love you Clem X.” ‘Brussels Is Haunted’ single and video Belgian filmmaker Jef De Smet directed the animated video for “Brussels Is Haunted,” which places the city’s monuments, historical events and past visitors alongside personal recollection. The video’s credits acknowledge the use of AI in portions of its imagery. Lyrically, the song sets Brussels landmarks and history, including Waterloo and the two world wars, against romance, nightlife and Belgian pop figure Plastic Bertrand. Speaking with MOJO magazine, McCulloch attributed part of the twelve-year gap between albums of new material to the pandemic, and said he wanted each song on “Apples for Isaac” to be, in his words, “cryptically important.” ‘Apples for Isaac’ tracklist and formats “Apples for Isaac” tracklist: Take Me By The Hand Can’t Be Sold Brussels Is Haunted I’ll Be Your Sunshine Hijacked The Honey Unstoppable Force The Light That Surrounds You Lab Rats Ran Asimov We Prayed In The Dark The album will be available on black vinyl, picture disc, signed test pressing, CD and digital formats, with clothing and tote-bag bundles also offered. Orders placed through the band’s store include an exclusive signed print. Pre-orders are open here. Echo & The Bunnymen tour dates for 2026 July 24-26 – Forest Fest, County Laois, Ireland August 7 – Fiesta de Begoña, Gijón, Spain August 8 – Festival Noroeste Estrella Galicia, A Coruña, Spain September 22 – Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, London, UK (sold out) September 23 – Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, London, UK December 20 – Barrowland Ballroom, Glasgow, UK December 22 – Barrowland Ballroom, Glasgow, UK Ticket information is available through the band’s official website. About Echo & The Bunnymen Echo & The Bunnymen formed in Liverpool in 1978 around vocalist Ian McCulloch, guitarist Will Sergeant and bassist Les Pattinson. Pete de Freitas joined as drummer in 1980. The band’s debut album, “Crocodiles,” reached the UK top 20 that year. “Heaven Up Here” followed in 1981. “Porcupine” reached number 2 on the UK Albums Chart in 1983 and produced the UK top 10 single “The Cutter.” “Ocean Rain,” released in 1984, included “The Killing Moon,” “Silver” and “Seven Seas.” McCulloch and Sergeant have continued to record as Echo & The Bunnymen through several later albums: “What Are You Going to Do with Your Life?” (1999), “Flowers” (2001), “Siberia” (2005), “The Fountain” (2009) and “Meteorites” (2014). “Apples for Isaac,” due September 18, 2026 on BMG, is the band’s thirteenth studio album and its first collection of newly written material in the twelve years since “Meteorites.”

items.body: Austrian futurepop project mind.in.a.box has announced its ninth studio album, “Retaliation”, due September 18, 2026. The album runs 13 tracks and 71 minutes. No lead single or video has been released from Retaliation yet. The tracklist: “Rebuild,” “Greatest Glory,” “Stoke the Fire,” “The Agency of Agony,” “We’ll Jump Together,” “Black Fog,” “Brother War,” “Little Miss Vicious,” “Toys,” “Stand and Rise,” “The Return,” “Retaliation,” and “Immunity.” mind.in.a.box’s cyberpunk story continues on ‘Retaliation’ The project is the sound, vocal and production work of Austrian musician Stefan Poiss, built around a continuing cyberpunk-themed story delivered through vocoder-processed vocals over futurepop and progressive trance production. Because 2010’s “R.E.T.R.O.” stands apart from that storyline, Retaliation is also the eighth chapter in the narrative that began with “Lost Alone,” following 2023’s “Black and White.” About mind.in.a.box Stefan Poiss and Markus Hadwiger, childhood friends from Austria, founded the band in Vienna in 2002. Poiss composes the music, sings and produces the records, while Hadwiger contributed to the project’s lyrics and story before becoming inactive; Poiss is now mind.in.a.box’s sole creative force. The debut album, “Lost Alone,” arrived in 2004 on Dependent Records (also released via Metropolis Records) and reached number one on the Deutsche Alternative Charts for five consecutive weeks. “Dreamweb” followed in 2005, peaking at number two on the same chart, and “Crossroads” arrived in September 2007, completing the project’s opening trilogy, later reissued together as the Dreamweb Trilogy 6LP box in 2020. In 2010, mind.in.a.box released “R.E.T.R.O.,” a release separate from its ongoing storyline that pays tribute to 8-bit computing and the Commodore 64. The project first performed live in 2009 at Sweden’s Arvika Festivalen, documented on the live album “Arvika Live” (2010). mind.in.a.box launched its own label, Dreamweb Music, for “Revelations,” released January 20, 2012, followed by “Memories” on March 20, 2015. “Broken Legacies,” released in 2017, was mind.in.a.box’s first album on THYX Records, Poiss’s own label, and its most recent album, “Black and White,” arrived August 30, 2023, also via THYX Records. “Retaliation” is set for September 18, 2026.

items.body: Swiss-German duo SIIE released the single “Indigo” via German label Cold Transmission Music on 17 July 2026. The coldwave and darkwave release arrives with an official music video and precedes a run of 2026 tour dates that include support for Nitzer Ebb. Cold Transmission Music describes “Indigo” as “a dreamlike journey through smoke, fading light, and fractured memories” that “drifts between French and German, blurring the line between longing, illusion, and memory.” The single holds two versions: the original track and an extended version. Indigo by SIIE SIIE also released an official music video for “Indigo,” shot by DOP Franz Schepers and published through Ed. Babelfish-Rückbank and Edition W-I-R-E. SIIE tour dates for 2026 following ‘Indigo’ release SIIE will give “Indigo” its live premiere at Amphi Festival in Cologne before a run of European dates that includes support slots on Nitzer Ebb’s 2026 tour: 26 July 2026 – Cologne, Germany – Amphi Festival (live premiere of “Indigo”) 5 September 2026 – Deutzen, Germany – NCN Festival 26 September 2026 – Nuremberg, Germany – MUZClub 7 November 2026 – Munich, Germany – Katzenclub 21 November 2026 – Halle, Germany – Capitol 19 December 2026 – Oberhausen, Germany – Kulttempel About SIIE SIIE is a German-Swiss electronic duo founded in 2021 and based in Hamburg, Germany. The project keeps its members anonymous to center attention on the music and visuals, mixing darkwave, techno and EBM with lyrics that have run from French into a French-and-German mix on “Indigo.” SIIE debuted in 2023 with a run of singles and videos through the US label Manta Recordings, featuring remixes by Panther Modern, Skelesys and Joyce Muniz. In 2024, the duo released the single “À Contre Jour” with Sian and Damon Jee on Joris Voorn’s Spectrum imprint, alongside the collaborative track “Violent” with Idoru. Its video for “Le Sept” placed third in the Performance category at the 2024 Berlin Music Video Awards, and SIIE began playing live that year, including dates at Berlin’s Kit Kat Club, Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig and Logo in Hamburg. SIIE signed to Cold Transmission Music in late 2024, releasing the introductory single “Grand Virage” that November and the second single “Cité Lunaire” in January 2025. Its debut album, “Acmé,” followed with ten tracks blending synthpop, EBM and dark-techno, released digitally and on CD on 2 May 2025 and on a limited 300-copy solid light pink vinyl pressing that June; Side-Line’s review rated the album 8 out of 10. SIIE issued the EP “Papier Glacé” on Cold Transmission Music later in 2025. “Indigo” is the duo’s newest single, released ahead of a European tour that includes 2026 support dates for Nitzer Ebb.

items.body: Review by tszirmay — This is a band that started out from the same progressive revival gates that spawned IQ, Marillion, Pallas and Pendragon back in the early 80s when prog was considered buried and dead by the fussy musical media. 1984 's "Journey to the East" had many interesting attributes that paralleled the above mentioned 'rebellious to change' lot, namely a superb lead vocalist in Mark Holliday, a masterful guitarist (Paul Ineson), David Powell offering some daring keyboard interventions and a tight rhythm section with a technically astounding bassist in Neil Duty. While there has been a fair number of revolving musicians coming and going , this 2026 recording has maintained the core of Holliday and Powell , as well as Duty (who has moved over to guitar duties), whilst adding Charlie Morgan on drums and Peter Robinson on bass (who had joined back in 1998 with the "Little Gods" album. Not always critically acclaimed because of labelling issues (the perennial neo-prog stamp often unfairly condemning the true Prog credentials). Well, that rather facile stigma may be soon erased, as this short album has only three epic tracks to further confound the criticism. The whopping title track spans a glorious 18 and a half minutes and should ,by any standards, cause a fair amount of consideration for positive objectivity. Allegedly, Neo is a simplified 'abacab' structure that relies on sedate musicianship whilst concentrating on ear-candy accessibility, hence the 5 minute and less structure, just perfect for radio play. From the very first notes, the pace shifts into symphonic overdrive, with a vast array of slight variations that would make most bands smile in amazement, Powell in particular inserting plenty of detail, providing Holliday to tell his tale with undisguised zeal. Yes, there is clear respect for the great lungs (Gabriel, Collins, Nicholson, Fish, Nicholls etc..), adding that touch of drama to the instrumental technique and it works when the arrangements keep the excitement levels pumping. Such is the case here, as the vocals convince completely. When all quiets down with only voice and piano, the magic seeps into the soul with no resistance possible. A swerving bass and subtle mellotron choir add the compulsory charm. A synth solo takes it straight into fantasy-land. At the midway point, the move to another level is achieved with faultless ease and conviction, squeezing as much restrained passion as possible. The instrumental work is on par with the very best this sub-genre has to offer, classy and illuminating, as if 'forged by the sun'. The electric guitar makes its entrance without attempting to hog the spotlight, tight teamwork is what characterizes this piece as well as the entire album, somehow reminding us of the great Genesis legacy (Trick and Wind in particular). Just in case it may be perceived as just a fanciful fluke , the 13 minute "Ceasefire For the Innocent" keeps the theatrics undeterred, albeit in a more pastoral setting to start. By closing my eyes for a moment, I had images of Ant Phillips' first solo album, both the artwork and music, very countrified English folk-prog that encapsulates profound lightness and a deep sense of feel good. A most welcome break (a ceasefire?) from all the toxic negativity one encounters by opening their phone or computer. Free at last, breathing in the air, admiring the glory of nature's gifts. Tingling piano here, distant guitar solemnity there, a serpentine synth slaloming in between, all the while guided by the pied-piper voice leading us into the verdant valleys of contentment. A few melancholic utterances in darker tones, exalt the power of wind, rain and storm, a welcome variation to the overall picture. Robinson's bass does some superb fills, even in the quietest moments, a subtility that cannot fail to surprise. To then revert back to majestic symphonism is what makes all of this piece shimmer with emotional deliverance, a chorale apotheosis to finish off in glory. One word: beautiful. The pleasant "Cue Rain" clocks in just over 6 minutes but still finds the way to seal the deal, dripping in romantic waves of joy. Holliday wows the microphone with a heavenly vocal performance, accompanied by delicate keyboard (piano and organ) ornamentations and a blues-jazz guitar line to die for, hints of vintage Procol Harum in more ways than one. So much far flippant classification, this is a charmingly attractive memento that truly deserves a fair shake, as it might just change the old prejudices once and for all. Its only fantastic music after all, and I love it. The gorgeous cover art adds to the enjoyment.4.5 Solar foundries
items._cn_summary: CASTANARC是1980年代新前卫摇滚复兴浪潮中的老牌乐队，2026年新专辑《Forged by the Sun》仅含三首长篇史诗曲目，其中同名曲长达18分半。乐评详细描述了其编制沿革——保留了核心成员Holliday与Powell，吸纳新鼓手与贝斯手。音乐风格承袭Marillion、IQ、Pendragon一脉，注重键盘编织与旋律人声结合，引用Genesis（特别是《Trick of the Tail》和《Wind & Wuthering》）作为参照。段落处理上从交响化过载段落过渡到钢琴人声静默，再以合成器独奏与低音线点缀。中段层次递进被认为'克制而充满激情'。整体被定位为对neo-prog陈旧标签的辩护，强调'真正的前卫资历'与团队协作的乐器技法。该类型在该用户关注的高实验性、爵士、电子等谱系中处于边缘地带，融合度低。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Bloodlines" is the seventh full-length studio album by Danish power metal act Pyramaze. The albumwas released through AFM Records in June 2023. It�s the successor to "Epitaph" from November 2020.Pyramaze is one man short since the release of "Epitaph" as guitarist Toke Skj�nnemand who had beena member since 2004 has left. Skj�nnemand has not been replaced and therefore Jacob Hansen performsall guitars and bass parts (and backing vocals) on "Bloodlines".Stylistically the material on "Bloodlines" continues the melodic and symphonic power metal sound ofthe preceding releases from Pyramaze. They still belong in the darker and heavier end of thesymphonic power metal spectrum, but the omnipresence of symphonic keyboards provide the music withan epic and polished quality. The sound production values further enhance that feeling. No matterhow heavy the riffs and drumming sometimes are they always take the backseat to the keyboards andthe vocals in the mix. On "Bloodlines" that is even more pronounced than earlier. The songwriting istop notch as always and the material is generally both effective and memorable, although maybe a bittoo vers/chorus formulaic and lacking a few unexpected twists and turn. A few compositionalsurprises would have been appreciated.When that is said "Bloodlines" is still a high quality release from Pyramaze in a by now long lineof quality releases. The album features a powerful, detailed, and epic sounding production job, themusicianship is on a high level on all posts, and the songwriting is professional and effective. A3.5 star (70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives.
items._cn_summary: 丹麦力量金属乐队Pyramaze第七张录音室专辑，延续其旋律化、交响化的力量金属路线。键盘音色在全作中占据主导地位，为编曲赋予史诗感和光泽感，即便吉他与鼓的段落偏重，也始终让位于键盘与人声。本作由Jacob Hansen一人包揽所有吉他、贝斯与和声部分，吉他手Toke Skjønnemand离队后未获补充。制作精良，编曲水准稳定，但在结构上偏向主歌-副歌的固定模式，缺少意料之外的转折与变化。作为一张制作成熟、技术在线的类型作品，整体听感专业而有效，但并未在风格边界上做出新的探索。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Recorded, once again, at Hollywood's Sound Factory under the production team of Larry and Fonce Mizell (Sky High) in November and December of 1974. Stepping into Tomorrow was released to the public in March of 1975.A1. "Stepping Into Tomorrow" (5:11) such simplicity! Please, say it ain't so! Luckily, it's a great, very catchy groove, otherwise there's more similarity to the music of later HERB ALPERT (1981's Rise) and the Blackbyrds (due to the choral vocals)--which is fine if you're heading toward radio-friendly pop-oriented "Smooth Jazz." I like the keyboard experimentations being done by Larry Mizell and Jerry Peters--and the vocals are actually quite a bit better (recorded/engineered) than those on the Blackbyrds' albums. Whoever is doing those ultra-soprano vocalese above the rest has got some pipes! (Lorraine Kenner? Stephanie Spruill?) (8.875/10)A2. "We're Together" (4:19) opening with an excellent and enticing "conversation" between Donald and Gary with piano, background female vocals, and background horns offering nice accents. I also like the scraping noise of the pick hitting the strings on the rhythm guitar. Unfortunately, the choir vocals end up occupying too much space: taking away from the instrumentalists. (8.875/10)B1. "Think Twice" (6:10) more vocal smoothation, this time with Team Male alternating with Team Female over some very simple jazz-funk (though with another great bass line and some nice vocal melodies). Jerry Peter's bouncy piano and Gary Bartz's smooth sax are nice complements to both the vocals and Donald's trumpet. (8.75/10)B2. "Rock And Roll Again" (6:09) smooth, smooth instrumental Soul music. Harkens back to the early 1960s in its simplicity. And there's that whistler dude James Carter who'll be so dominant on Side Two of the next album (Places and Spaces). Otherwise, this is really just a classic soul/DooWap tune on which the alto sax takes the place of the human voice. Donald must be feeling really nostalgic. (8.66667/10)C2. "I Love The Girl" (3:53) piano and gentle percussion instruments open this before the band engages in some cinematic Burt Bacharach-like music behind James Carter's whistling. When Donald kicks in with his flugelhorn in the second minute it is over some loose funk in which laid back yet playful bass and steady drums amuse beneath Jerry's wildly-adventurous piano play. It's kind of shame that his piano is mixed so far back into the mix cuz it's really entertaining and interesting. (8.75/10)C3. "You Are The World" (4:29) bongos, timbales, and two fast-strummed rhythm guitar chords repeated over and over precede the "you are the world" male choir pronouncements. Then the music travels into a funkier BARRY WHITE world with piano and wildly flailing wah-wah chord fast-strumming rhythm guitar. This is definitely early Disco. I don't dislike it; it feels so ready for radio! (Especially in Detroit town!) (9/10)D2. "Design A Nation" (4:21) very pleasant Smooth Jazz with very relaxing vocal choir work, whispered female voice, smooth sax from Gary Bartz, and a great bass-led groove at its foundation. (9/10)D3. "Makin' It" (3:49) a song with a little more zip and jazz in it despite the funk/R&B presentation. Jew's harp, piano, clavinet, and percussion are key components beneath Donald and Gary's horns. (It has elements that sound quite a bit like Ronnie Laws' monster hit--also from 1975, "Always There.") I like the lively spirit of those contribution to the foundation. (9/10)The master of borrowing riffs and sounds from past masters has been caught: it's no longer working its magic as it once had. Is just my ears or has Chuck Rainey's bass playing (and volume) been curbed or downscaled from the levels and freedoms expressed on the previous album? I think this an unfortunate mistake on the part of both the composer, bandleader, and producers.Total time: 39:21B/four stars; an excellent album of simplified Jazz-Rock Fusion that finds portents of Disco, Jazz-Funk, and Smooth Jazz in its weaves.
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年录音的专辑由Larry和Fonce Mizell制作，在好莱坞Sound Factory完成，整体走的是旋律顺滑、节奏明快的放克与灵魂乐路线，带有早期迪斯科的影子。评论者指出曲风偏向电台友好型平滑爵士，编曲相对简洁，强调人声合唱、钢琴、贝斯线条和萨克斯的搭配，Donald Byrd的小号和flugelhorn时有出场，但器乐部分往往让人声合唱占据太多空间。评论中对Jerry Peters活泼的钢琴演奏评价较高，但对混音中钢琴被压低表示遗憾。歌曲取材广泛，从Burt Bacharach式的电影化配乐到Barry White风格的放克均有涉及。整体而言，这张专辑更偏向主流商业化制作，与实验性、前卫性音乐的关系较为疏远。

items.body:
The first volume in a series revisiting Theo's infamous Ugly Edits bootleg series - an officially licensed version after those mad collectible hand-sprayed first editions in 2002. 

"Following Chicago’s tradition in special edits and dj personal reworks to extend crucial parts and surprise the dancers, Theo Parrish has always sparkled his legendary sets with his own versions of classic and obscure disco, funk and soul cuts to maximum effect! Some of those were available to fans in mid 2000s via the Ugly Edits series, now it’s finally time for the LOVELY EDITS.

Officially licensed and using the original parts from the master tapes, here we have Theo’s takes on two absolute staples: BT EXPRESS ‘Peace Pipe’ and GEORGE DUKE ‘I Want You For Myself’.""
items._cn_summary: 这是Theo Parrish对经典放克与灵魂乐作品的重新编辑版本，源自其2002年著名的地下Ugly Edits混音系列。本次官方授权发行采用了原始母带音源，收录了BT Express的《Peace Pipe》与George Duke的《I Want You For Myself》两首作品的重新演绎，延续了芝加哥DJ传统中对经典段落进行延伸与重组的手法，以服务舞池效果为核心目的。整体内容偏向舞曲文化背景下的实用型编辑作品，与实验、前卫或电子前沿领域的探索关联较弱，乐评文本较短且以介绍性质为主，缺乏对声音设计或艺术理念的深入分析。

items.body:
Gathering the short-lived Boston emo outfit's influential debut 'Junk', shoegaze-y sophomore album 'This Afternoon Malady', the unfinished third album and everything in-between, 'Wait A Lifetime' will be crucial listening if you're more than a casual Jejune fan.

Jejune were never the Berklee-educated New England scene's best band, but they proved their mettle all the same, penning a pair of albums that almost inadvertently steered the course of the emo underground. Those records aren't without their faults, sure, but it's hard to get an accurate read on the US scene without them. And they've never sounded better; with a fresh lick of paint, 'Junk' and its superior, if way more misunderstood follow-up deserves to be filed alongside Karate's early records at the very least. And for the heads, 'Wait A Lifetime' sweeps up all the band's recorded material, the loose singles, split EPs and compilation tracks, even excavating the sessions from their aborted third album and commissioning an essay from critic Nina Corcoran to fill in the gaps.

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Epitaph" is the sixth full-length studio album by Danish power metal act Pyramaze. The album wasreleased through AFM Records in November 2020. It�s the successor to "Contingent" from April 2017and it�s now the third album in a row featuring the same quintet lineup. It�s interesting to notethat two of the band�s former lead vocalists guests (Matt Barlow and Lance King) on the closing12:04 minutes long "The Time Traveller".If you�re familiar with the last couple of releases from Pyramaze you won�t fall off your chair witha surprised expression on your face when listening to "Epitaph" as it follows a similar heavy andsymphonic power metal path as the previous releases. It�s maybe slightly heavier and darker than"Contingent", but on the other hand "Contingent" was a pretty dark and heavy power metal releaseitself, so it�s probably just my ears toying with me. In this case dark and heavy doesn�t meaninaccessible or that Pyramaze are leaning towards any form of extreme metal, just that they belongin the heavier end of the symphonic power metal spectrum. The material is generally still verymelodic, epic in nature, and featuring a polished and detailed sound production.Heavy guitars and drumming, are complimented by omnipresent symphonic keyboards and the strongvocals by Terje Har�y. Pyramaze are arguably an incredibly skilled unit and they know how to writean intriguing and powerful song too. Most tracks follow a relatively normal vers/chorus structurebut the above mentioned "The Time Traveller" is a progressive metal tracks where Pyramaze get toshow that they can leave the vers/chorus formula songwriting when they want to. With no less thanfour vocalists performing on "The Time Traveller" (the last one being Brittney Hayes from Unleashthe Archers) and more room for Pyramaze to play instrumental parts (although the tracks is mostlyvocal-centric) "The Time Traveller" is arguably one of the highlights of "Epitaph" and a standouttrack in their discography.Upon conclusion Pyramaze have released another high quality symphonic power metal album as "Epitaph"features both high level musicianship, a powerful and detailed production job, and some solid genretypical songwriting featuring a lot of compositional details. It�s effective and memorable. A 3.5star (70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._cn_summary: 丹麦乐队Pyramaze第六张专辑延续其交响力量金属路线，编曲厚重型，键盘铺陈密集，人声强劲。整体风格较前作略重略暗，但仍属该类型光谱中较重的常规作品。12分钟长篇曲目由四位主唱合作，包含前任歌手回归，结构较为自由，被视为专辑亮点。其余曲目大多遵循主歌副歌格式，歌曲写作扎实但未呈现明显实验性或跨界元素，制作精良而工整。作为一张类型内的稳健作品，在高水准器乐演奏与精致制作方面值得肯定，但对偏好实验、前卫或融合风格而言缺乏足够的艺术突破。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — I am not quite sure as to whether to view this as a new studio recording or a compilation, or both, as what we have here is a combination of unheard recordings, newly reworked classics and fresh material from the current line-up, and I am not sure exactly who plays on what. I am aware that the vibrant and upbeat "Hurry On Sundown" is the final recording to feature Huw Lloyd- Langton, who left the band in 2002 and died from cancer in 2012, but have no information as to where and when it was recorded.Hawkwind as a band have probably suffered more than most from having compilations released over which they have had no control, along with many live recordings (some of which have poor sound quality at best), so much so that anyone who says they have a complete collection is either lying or demented, which means that there is always a certain level of trepidation when approaching any of their albums which have been compiled. However, this is a fascinating viewpoint into one particular style of their music, with new songs such as "Four Legs Good, Two Legs Bad" and "There Are Fairies In The Garden" happily sitting alongside reimagined versions of the likes of "The Demented Man" and "Those Days Of The Underground". The former is one of the highlights on the album, and it is difficult to think that the original take was on 'Warrior on the Edge of Time' which is now more than 50 years old. This still has an acoustic guitar at its base, but feels vita and modern. The album also includes tracks drawn from associated projects, including Dave Brock's unreleased 'Dance and Trance' material ("Land Of Min", "Out Of Luck") and Magnus Martin's "Ocean's Spiral", but the absolute highlight is a driving live-in-the-studio take on "PSI Power", which was originally the opening track on '25 Years On' and has long been one of my favourites. Here it is still high energy and clearly demonstrates the current line-up is continuing to add to the legacy, even though David Brock is now 84 years old and still shows no sign at all of slowing down either recording or gigging. This is a set any fan of the band will thoroughly enjoy.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / hard rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Hawkwind乐队2026年的精选作品，混合了未发表录音、经典曲目重新编曲版本以及当前阵容的新作品。专辑包含已故吉他手Huw Lloyd-Langton的最终录音，也收录了Dave Brock未发表的'Dance and Trance'素材以及Magnus Martin的作品。重新演绎的曲目如'The Demented Man'在原声吉他基础上呈现出更具现代感的活力，而现场录音版本的'PSI Power'则展示了84岁的David Brock仍然保持的高能量创作状态。整体而言，这是一张面向乐队忠实粉丝的合辑，介于新录音与精选之间，试图呈现乐队某一特定风格的演进历程。

items.body: Joy Division released their second and final studio album, “Closer,” on 18 July 1980 through Factory Records. The album turns 46 this year. “Closer” arrived two months after the death of singer Ian Curtis, who was found dead on 18 May 1980, and it remains the band’s last release before the surviving members regrouped as New Order. The Manchester post-punk band recorded “Closer” between 18 and 30 March 1980 at Britannia Row Studios in Islington, London, produced by Martin Hannett, with Jon Caffery as engineer. The nine-track album is sequenced across two sides: “Atrocity Exhibition,” “Isolation,” “Passover,” “Colony” and “A Means to an End” open the record, followed by “Heart and Soul,” “Twenty Four Hours,” “The Eternal” and “Decades.” “Closer” streams on Spotify. About Joy Division Joy Division began in Salford, England, in 1976 as Warsaw, formed by Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook after seeing a Sex Pistols concert. Ian Curtis joined as vocalist, and Stephen Morris completed the lineup on drums. The band changed its name to Joy Division in 1978 to avoid confusion with the London band Warsaw Pakt, and signed to Tony Wilson’s newly founded Factory Records the same year. Factory Records released the debut album “Unknown Pleasures” in June 1979, produced by Martin Hannett, whose production style became closely associated with the band’s sound. Joy Division toured the UK and Europe through 1979 and early 1980 while Curtis, who had been diagnosed with epilepsy, performed under increasing strain from his condition and its treatment. The band recorded its second album, “Closer,” at Britannia Row Studios in March 1980. Curtis died on 18 May 1980, the day before the band was due to leave for its first North American tour. Factory released “Closer” on 18 July 1980, alongside the single “Love Will Tear Us Apart,” which had been issued the previous month. Sumner, Hook and Morris continued as New Order later in 1980, joined by keyboardist Gillian Gilbert, and released their debut album “Movement” on Factory in 1981. Joy Division’s two studio albums, along with the compilations “Still” (1981) and “Substance” (1988), remain in circulation through Factory-successor reissues. The band’s story, including the making of “Closer,” was documented in “Joy Division” (2007) and dramatized in “Control” (2007). The anniversary of “Closer” places the album back in Joy Division’s timeline as the record that closed the band’s original run and opened the way to New Order.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非真正的乐评，而是一篇纪念性新闻稿，介绍了Joy Division第二张也是最后一张录音室专辑《Closer》发行46周年。文章主要罗列了唱片的基本信息：1980年7月18日由Factory Records发行，3月在伦敦Britannia Row Studios录制，Martin Hannett担任制作人，九首曲目分布在A、B两面。文章还简述了乐队从Warsaw到Joy Division的演变、主唱Ian Curtis因癫痫恶化去世的经过，以及余下成员后来组建New Order的历程，并提及了相关纪录片和传记电影。全文缺乏对专辑音乐本体、声音设计、歌词主题或制作手法的任何分析性评价，也未探讨专辑在后朋克与暗潮美学中的历史定位。对于关注实验、前卫或暗潮音乐的听众而言，这篇内容提供的信息密度极低，更像是一份按时间线整理的事实清单，而非具有深度的音乐评论。

items.body: German gothic rock band MONO INC. will release the best-of album “20 Years of Darkness” on November 27, 2026, via NoCut Entertainment/SPV. The 32-track collection spans songs from 2003 to 2023 and is completed by three new, previously unreleased songs, led by the new single “Herzblut.” The release follows MONO INC.’s third consecutive number-one German album, “Darkness,” released in 2025. “20 Years of Darkness” is available for pre-order in four formats: a limited Fan Box, Silver Marbled 3-LP vinyl, Black 3-LP vinyl, and 2-CD Digipak, plus a 2-CD-and-T-shirt bundle, through MONO INC.’s official shop. MONO INC. ’20 Years of Darkness’ tracklist Confirmed tracklist: “Comedown,” “Wave No Flag,” “Mondschein,” “C’est La Vie,” “In The End,” “The Raven’s Back,” “Herzblut,” “Radio Mono,” “Torture Me,” “Shelter,” “Forever and a Day,” “Rest in Grace,” “Why Can’t I,” “Ich teile dich nicht,” “Forever,” “Twice in Life,” “The Best of You,” “Burn Me,” “When the Raven Dies Tonight,” “Herzschlag,” “Tired of the Day,” “Never Say Die,” “It Never Rains,” “Bloodmoon,” “This Is My Life,” “Mein Herz,” “Grown,” “The Promise,” “Feuer,” “Under a Coal Black Sun,” “Euthanasia,” and “One Time In Your Life.” The best-of arrives in the middle of a run of MONO INC. open-air shows across Germany: Saturday, July 25 – Cologne, Germany – Amphi Festival (Tanzbrunnen) Friday, August 7 – Bremen, Germany – Seebühne Rockt 4.0 Saturday, August 8 – Schwerin, Germany – Pappelpark Open Air Saturday, August 15 – Magdeburg, Germany – Festung Mark Friday, August 21 – Dinslaken, Germany – Freilichtbühne Saturday, August 22 – Hanau, Germany – Amphitheater Friday, August 28 – Potsdam, Germany – Waschhaus Open Air Saturday, August 29 – Klaffenbach, Germany – Wasserschloss About MONO INC. Miky Mono (vocals, bass), Carl Fornia (guitar) and Martin Engler (drums) formed MONO INC. in Hamburg, Germany, in 2000. Bassist Manuel Antoni joined in 2003 as the band self-released its debut album, “Head Under Water.” MONO INC. signed to NoCut Entertainment in 2004 and reissued “Head Under Water” with new artwork, spawning the singles “Burn Me” and “Superman.” Engler moved to lead vocals in 2006, with Katha Mia joining on drums; the pair’s first album together, “Temple of the Torn,” followed in 2007. “Pain, Love & Poetry” (2008) included a duet with Lisa Middelhauve of Xandria, and “Voices of Doom” followed in 2009, the year MONO INC. toured with Subway to Sally and ASP. Founding singer Miky Mono died in a paragliding accident in October 2010. MONO INC. released “Viva Hades” in March 2011 and signed to SPV/Rookies & Kings the following year, releasing “After the War” in 2012. “Nimmermehr” (2013) reached number three on the German charts, followed by the compilation “The Clock Ticks On 2004-2014” in 2014 and “Terlingua” in 2015. “Together Till the End” (2017) and the compilation “Symphonies of Pain” preceded “Welcome to Hell” (2018) and “The Book of Fire” (2020), which reached number one in Germany. MONO INC.’s twelfth studio album, “Ravenblack,” followed in 2023, also topping the German charts. Bassist Ilja John Lappin joined in 2025, replacing Val Perun, the same year MONO INC. released its 13th studio album, “Darkness,” which became the band’s third consecutive number-one album in Germany and was followed by an October 2025 tour. MONO INC.’s current lineup is Martin Engler (vocals), Carl Fornia (guitar, backing vocals), Katha Mia (drums, backing vocals) and Ilja John Lappin (bass). “20 Years of Darkness,” due November 27, 2026, gathers songs from across the band’s catalog alongside new material.
items._cn_summary: 这是关于德国哥特摇滚乐队MONO INC.即将发行精选专辑"20 Years of Darkness"的新闻稿。专辑定于2026年11月27日通过NoCut Entertainment/SPV发行，收录2003至2023年间共32首曲目，包括三首此前未发表的新歌及主打单曲"Herzblut"。发行形式涵盖限量粉丝盒、黑胶、CD Digipak及T恤套装等多种版本。文章还列举了乐队的夏季露天巡演日程，并简要回顾了乐队从2000年汉堡成立至今的成员变动与厂牌签约历程。整体内容属于典型的商业新闻通稿，缺乏对音乐本身的艺术分析、创作语境探讨或听觉特征描述。

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.

items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦于Miles Davis与John Coltrane合作历程中贝斯手的更替线索，以Paul Chambers为核心人物展开叙述。文章梳理了Chambers从底特律Cass Technical高中起步、赴纽约发展、加入Davis和Coltrane阵营的轨迹，以及他在Kind of Blue、Giant Steps、Sketches of Spain等经典录音中的参与情况。行文偏重编年史式的事实陈述，涵盖录音日期、巡演安排和合作者名单，信息密度较高但缺乏对音乐本体——和声走向、节奏语言、即兴结构——的分析。文章截稿于Chambers之后接替进入Davis乐团的另一位底特律出身贝斯手，内容尚不完整。整体定位为主流爵士史回顾，与实验、前卫或电子融合方向距离较远。
